findings: PhysicalInput classifies external incidence as Sample or Transition while preserving the same ordinary drive path; only the opt-in protocol reads transition eligibility for consequence.
Causal lineage preserves an optional transition tick per anonymous physical origin through merging, selection, propagation, checkpoint save, and exact replay.
For the same later origin, Sample produced typed RejectedUnchangedSample with no consequence write, while Transition was admitted and consequential.

The hand adapter records sample and transition incidence plus transition eligibility in its reusable whole-decision evidence without exposing position, direction, contact, desired action, or hand identity to the learner.

The local discriminator survived: origins 10001, 10002, and 10004 were admitted on physical transition and rejected on later sampling; seventy-six unchanged samples were rejected with exact replay, natural quiescence, and zero propagation exhaustion.
Stable active-member novelty was falsified by two actual movements with the same active-origin set.

Hand release was falsified: after false writes stopped, the silent motor retained path inputs but had zero projected drive, remained non-executable, and never fired; the candidate retained four position changes and upper clamp.
All 55 non-ignored core tests passed, two adversarial tests remained explicitly ignored, all parent and candidate experiment tests passed, and the independent warm loop completed in 0.04 seconds.
residual_uncertainty: The opt-in physical-transition protocol is locally supported discovery physics, not default behavior or organism authority.
Correct transition classification is an explicit external physical boundary; worlds whose physical sensors cannot expose change remain observationally unable to distinguish it.
The hand remains unsolved. The next localized frontier is one bounded unanswered-return opportunity reaching a fresh local alternative before path-sign cancellation and executability.
